result.markdown: --- title: "Niche partitioning between planktivorous fish in the pelagic Baltic Sea assessed by DNA metabarcoding, qPCR and microscopy" author: - name: Andreas Novotny orcid: 0000-0001-8910-6183 affiliations: - Institute for the Oceans and Fisheries, The University of British Columbia, Vancouver, Canada - Department of Ecology, Environment, and Plant Sciences, Stockholm University, Stockholm, Sweden - name: Kinlan MG Jan orcid: 0000-0002-5579-0017 affiliations: - Department of Ecology, Environment, and Plant Sciences, Stockholm University, Stockholm, Sweden - name: Jan Dierking orcid: 0000-0002-4660-6919 affiliations: - GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel, Kiel, Germany - name: Monika Winder orcid: 0000-0001-9467-3035 affiliations: - Department of Ecology, Environment, and Plant Sciences, Stockholm University, Stockholm, Sweden Year: "2022" doi: "https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-15116-7" Journal: Scientific Reports categories: - "Fish" - "Zooplankton" - "Niche" - "Food-web" - "DNA metabarcoding" - "qPCR" - "Microscopy" --- ::: {.cell} ::: Marine communities undergo rapid changes related to human-induced ecosystem pressures. The Baltic Sea pelagic food web has experienced several regime shifts during the past century, resulting in a system where competition between the dominant planktivorous mesopredatory clupeid fish species herring (Clupea harengus) and sprat (Sprattus sprattus) and the rapidly increasing stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus) population is assumed to be high. Here, we investigate diet overlap between these three planktivorous fishes in the Baltic Sea, utilizing DNA metabarcoding on the 18S rRNA gene and the COI gene, targeted qPCR, and microscopy. Our results show niche differentiation between clupeids and stickleback, and highlight that rotifers play an important role in this pattern, as a resource that is not being used by the clupeids nor by other zooplankton in spring. We further show that all the diet assessment methods used in this study are consistent, but also that DNA metabarcoding describes the plankton-fish link at the highest taxonomic resolution. This study suggests that rotifers and other understudied soft-bodied prey may have an important function in the pelagic food web and that the growing population of pelagic stickleback may be supported by the open feeding niche offered by the rotifers. A Novotny, KMG Jan, J Dierking, M Winder. 2022. Niche partitioning between planktivorous fish in the pelagic Baltic Sea assessed by DNA metabarcoding, qPCR and microscopy. Scientific Reports. 12 (1), 10952.
